title: tcspecial configuration, version 2
description: The shape of a version 2 configuration: which sections there are, what an entry may say, and which words are words. Not whether it can be flown -- which attributes a node of a given type must state, whether two payloads claim one socket, whether a mean's inputs are the ones its links bind are rules about meaning, tested against real buses, and tcsverify is the one place they live. A file this accepts may still be refused, and the refusal will say why.

linkEntry.description: One line out of a node: the node it goes to, and which of that node's inputs it feeds where it feeds a named one. One entry per line, so several lines are several entries and nothing pairs by position.

target.description: The node this line goes to.

input.description: Which of that node's inputs the line feeds, or which of its data sinks it arrives at, where either has to be said.

version.description: Which language this file is written in. A configuration that has not said has not said what it is, and the beacon carries it so the ground can check what is flying.

include.description: Other files this one is made of, by name without an extension: named rather than discovered, so the set of files a configuration is made of is itself written down.

tcspecial.description: What tcspecial itself is configured with: where commands are taken, where beacons go, where the telemetry log is written. Everything optional here, because the editor has to be able to write a section somebody is halfway through filling in; what must be answered before a configuration flies is tcsverify's to say.

recv.description: Where tcspecial receives commands about the spacecraft and sends its responses.

send.description: Where the MOC sends them from and receives the responses.

source_base.description: The MOC's end, counted on by the payload's id.

dest_base.description: tcspecial's end, counted on by the payload's id.

source_base.description: Where a payload's telemetry leaves tcspecial, counted on by its id.

dest_base.description: Where it arrives at the ground, counted on by its id.

interval_ms.description: How often a beacon is sent.

send.description: The socket tcspecial sends beacons from.

recv.description: The socket tcsmoc receives them on.

payload_groups.description: Sets of payloads read on one interval, so that readings which will be compared are taken as close to together as the hardware allows.

interval.description: A whole number and a unit, written together: 500ms, 3s, 15m, 6h, 1w. The units are us, ms, s, m, h, d and w, matched longest first, so 500ms is milliseconds and 500m is minutes. The number may be decimal or hexadecimal with an 0x prefix, with underscores among the digits: 1_000ms and 0x3e8ms are 1000ms.

moc.description: The ground links: what the editor's moc working pane holds.

name.description: What this node is called, unique across the configuration.

type.description: What it is: the configuration's own word for the type.

group.description: The payload group that reads it, where it is in one.

payload-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `payload-out`, one entry each. An entry names the node the line goes to as its `target`, and `input` where it feeds a named input of that node. The short spellings are read too: the destination as a string, `node` or `node.terminal`, alone or in a list.

One line, written as the node it reaches: `node` or `node.terminal`.

moc-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `moc-out`, one entry each. An entry names the node the line goes to as its `target`, and `input` where it feeds a named input of that node. payload-in.description: Whether a line arrives at this node's `payload-in` sink. A record of the links written on the nodes they leave, and not a link: which node a line comes from is written on that node. A file may leave it out; one that disagrees with the links is refused where it is read.

moc-in.description: Whether a line arrives at this node's `moc-in` sink. A record of the links written on the nodes they leave, and not a link: which node a line comes from is written on that node. A file may leave it out; one that disagrees with the links is refused where it is read.

ground_base.description: Where the ground station is, as address:port. What each node linked into this moc node produces is sent to that address, at that port plus the node's device id.

vehicle.description: What the vehicle itself runs: computations, logs, pass-throughs, pages of their own.

program.description: The program a node runs: an app node's application, or the program of a `process` computation. An app node's is executed with `~` and `$HOME` expanded as a shell would expand them, and with the node's name as its first argument.

app-payload-arg.description: What an app node's program is told about the payload stream, as the argument after the node's name. Said by the kinds that handle payload data -- app_payload_veh, app_all_veh, app_pl, app_all_pl -- and required of them, the arguments being a fixed list.

from.description: The MOC link it arrives on.

tcsgui.description: What the editor arranged: where each node was drawn. Last in the file and in a section of its own, because the sections above say what the vehicle carries and this says where somebody put the boxes on a screen. The flight software ignores it.
